patch.description: Turning it on generates a data key, wraps it under the key-encryption key and stores it; turning it off retires the active key. Neither takes effect instantly: for `ENCRYPTION_KEY_RING_REFRESH_INTERVAL_MS` the previous state keeps governing new writes so every engine process learns of the change first. From the change onward the background sweep moves every stored onboarding toward the chosen state — encrypting plain JSON rows, or decrypting every row back to plain JSON — with no further operator action. Idempotent: asking for the state that already holds changes nothing. Returns the resulting state, as `GET` would.

patch.description: Stores the automatic-rotation schedule on the active key, or clears it with `null`. The next rotation is always the active key's creation plus this interval, never this request's own instant, so choosing an interval shorter than the active key's age makes it due immediately and the engine rotates on its next check (`ENCRYPTION_KEY_ROTATION_CHECK_INTERVAL_MS`). A rotation — scheduled or asked for with `POST /keys` — creates a key that carries the same schedule forward and restarts the countdown from its own creation. Turning encryption on schedules no rotation at all. Idempotent: choosing the interval already in force changes nothing. Returns the resulting state, as `GET` would.

post.description: Generates a new key, wraps it under the key-encryption key, retires the active key and inserts the new one in one transaction, then reloads the local key ring. The new key does not become active immediately: for up to `ENCRYPTION_KEY_RING_REFRESH_INTERVAL_MS` it is reported as `pendingActivation` while the previous key keeps protecting new writes, so every engine process has a chance to learn of it first. Stored onboardings are not rewritten: rotation is lazy, so a row keeps naming the key it was written under and moves onto this one only the next time it is written. The new key carries the automatic-rotation schedule the superseded one had, and the countdown to the next scheduled rotation restarts from this key's creation. Returns only the new key's id — never its material.

post.description: Records a standing request for the background sweep to move every stored onboarding onto the active key, including rows still naming a superseded one. Rotation alone does not do this: it changes which key new writes use and leaves stored rows where they are until something rewrites them. This is the answer to a data key whose material leaked, where those rows must stop naming it without waiting. The work is a batch per sweep tick, each row decrypted and re-encrypted inside one transaction, so no row is ever stored as plain JSON on the way across — unlike turning encryption off and on again, which writes every onboarding to disk unencrypted in between. `progress.pending` counts rows not yet on the active key for as long as the request stands, and the sweep clears it once none are left. Idempotent: asking again while one stands re-stamps it and changes nothing else.

post.description: A provider's asynchronous result for a connector step. The engine verifies the HMAC the adapter declares over the raw body first, maps the payload to the onboarding it belongs to and to step data, and then submits that data exactly as the flow's submit route would, so the same workflow outcomes and the same refusals apply. A replay of a callback already applied is acknowledged and ignored.

requestBody.description: The provider's payload, byte for byte as the provider sent it: the signature is computed over exactly these bytes, so the body is read raw and parsed only after it verifies. The signature and timestamp header names are whatever the connector adapter declares for its provider.

400.description:
`ASYNC_CALLBACK_RAW_BODY_REQUIRED`: The callback arrived without a body the signature could be verified over.

`ASYNC_CALLBACK_PROVIDER_KEY_INVALID`: The provider key is not made of lower-case letters, digits and underscores.

`ASYNC_CALLBACK_AUTHENTICATION_FAILED`: No connector adapter that accepts callbacks is registered under this provider key.

`INVALID_STEP_DATA`: The submitted data violates the current step; `errors` maps each refused field to its reasons, and the onboarding stays where it was.

401.description: `ASYNC_CALLBACK_SIGNATURE_INVALID`: The signature could not be verified: the header is missing or malformed, the digest does not match, the timestamp is missing or outside the tolerance, or the connector is not allowed to send unsigned callbacks.

`SUMSUB_UNAVAILABLE`: Sumsub could not be reached, or answered with an error the adapter does not map to an outcome.

`VERIFF_UNAVAILABLE`: Veriff could not be reached, or answered with an error the adapter does not map to an outcome.

info.title: TSH Onboarding Conductor Engine API
info.description:
The HTTP surface of the onboarding engine: the service that loads workflow definitions, runs
onboardings against them and drives connectors, provider callbacks and client webhooks.

## Audiences

- **Onboarding flow.** The end customer's own onboarding. Unauthenticated: the onboarding id is
  the only handle, so treat it as a capability.
- **Admin.** The operator surface the admin panel is built on. Every operation requires a bearer
  access token (see *Authentication*).
- **Provider callbacks.** Where a connector's provider posts an asynchronous result, authenticated
  by the HMAC recipe the connector adapter declares.

## Authentication

Admin operations carry the `entraBearer` security requirement: a Microsoft Entra ID
access token for the engine's API app registration whose `roles` claim holds at least one of the
configured operator roles. A missing or unverifiable token is answered with `401`, a verified token
without an operator role with `403`, and `503` says the token could not be judged because Entra's
signing keys were unreachable. Every decision, granted or refused, is written to the audit log.

## Errors

The engine answers a refusal it owns with `{ "code", "message" }`: `code` is the stable
identifier a client should branch on, and each operation lists the codes it can return. Some codes
add detail properties; the operation's response description names them. Where the framework answers
instead of the engine, the body is NestJS's own `{ "statusCode", "message", "error" }` envelope:
request validation (`400`), the admin bearer guard (`401`, `403`, `503`), and a `500` on the
submit and provider-callback routes, where a connector adapter can fail with a plain error and there
is no `code` to branch on.

## Bodies the workflow decides

Two request bodies have no fixed shape. A submit body follows the current step: read
`GET /v1/onboardings/{id}/state` and its `step.schema` says exactly what the engine will accept.
A connector's settings body is a map whose keys the connector adapter declares; the read side lists
them. The compile body is a workflow document, and its schema is embedded here in full.

## About this document

Generated from the engine's own route and DTO decorators, and committed beside the code; a test
fails when the two disagree. A running engine serves it at `GET /v1/openapi.json`.

tags.name: Health
tags.description: Liveness for orchestration and load balancers. Unauthenticated.

tags.name: Onboarding flow
tags.description: The end customer's own onboarding: start it, read the step to render, submit that step's data, upload the documents a step asks for and accept an agreement version it owes. These routes carry no authentication because an end customer holds no operator identity; the onboarding id is the only handle, so treat it as a capability and never log or share it.

tags.name: Manual review
tags.description: An operator's decision on an onboarding waiting in `awaiting_manual_review`. Unauthenticated today, unlike the rest of the operator surface: the route predates admin sign-in and has not been moved behind it. Treat this as a known gap rather than a design intent, and keep a network boundary in front of the engine's port.

tags.name: Provider callbacks
tags.description: Asynchronous results a provider posts back after a connector step. Authenticated by the HMAC recipe the connector adapter declares (header names, digest, encoding, timestamp tolerance), verified over the raw body before anything else happens to the request.

tags.name: Admin: onboardings
tags.description: Operator reads over every onboarding: the paginated list, one record, the states it moved through and the agreements it holds, plus the one write that links a published agreement version to it. Requires an operator bearer token.

tags.name: Admin: agreements
tags.description: The published versions of every agreement family: publish the next version of one, which links it as pending to every onboarding now behind, and list what has been published. Requires an operator bearer token.

tags.name: Admin: workflows
tags.description: The workflow catalogue as a reader sees it, and a dry compile of a document that stores nothing. Requires an operator bearer token.

tags.name: Admin: step types
tags.description: The step palette a workflow builder offers and the JSON Schema an authored workflow document must satisfy. Requires an operator bearer token.

tags.name: Admin: connectors
tags.description: Operator-provided connector settings, including credentials. A secret value never leaves the engine: the read side reports that a secret is set, not what it is. Requires an operator bearer token.

tags.name: Admin: audit
tags.description: The paginated audit log with its filters. Requires an operator bearer token.

tags.name: Admin: encryption
tags.description: Encryption of `onboardings.context`: whether it is on, the key history with derived sweep progress, the switch that turns it on or off, and the write that rotates the key. A response never carries key material. Requires an operator bearer token.

entraBearer.description: A Microsoft Entra ID access token issued for the engine API app registration (`AZURE_API_AUDIENCE`), carrying at least one of the roles in `ADMIN_REQUIRED_ROLES`. With `ADMIN_AUTH_ENABLED=false`, a local-only setting the engine refuses in production, the guard is skipped and no token is needed.

id.description: The id written into every envelope this key produced.

createdBy.description: The operator who turned encryption on or added this key, as the bearer token identified them, or the unknown-actor marker when admin authentication is off. Null only for a row inserted outside the API; every key the engine creates records who asked for it.

activatedAt.description: When this key becomes (or became) the active one. May be in the future — see `pendingActivation`.

deletedAt.description: When this key stops (or stopped) protecting new writes — superseded by a rotation or retired by turning encryption off; null while it has not been. May be in the future: the key stays `active` until then.

active.description: Whether this is the key `encrypt` currently uses.

pendingActivation.description: Whether this key has been added but has not activated yet — `activatedAt` is still in the future, during the grace window that gives every replica a chance to learn of it before anything encrypts with it. The previous key remains `active` until then.

EncryptionKeyRotationInterval.description: How often the engine rotates the encryption key on its own, measured from the active key's creation: 48 or 96 hours, one or two weeks, or a fixed 30-day month.

interval.description: How often the engine rotates the key on its own; `null` when it does not, and while encryption is off.

nextRotationAt.description: When the next automatic rotation falls due: the active key's `createdAt` plus `interval`. Null whenever `interval` is. In the past for a schedule that has come due but whose rotation the engine has not run yet — it checks every `ENCRYPTION_KEY_ROTATION_CHECK_INTERVAL_MS`.

pending.description: Onboardings not yet in the chosen state: stored as plain JSON while encryption is on, still encrypted while it is off. A row on a superseded key is not pending — rotation is lazy, so it moves to the current key the next time it is written.

enabled.description: Whether encryption is turned on: a key exists that has not been retired. `true` from the moment an operator turns it on, including the grace window before that key activates (`keys[].pendingActivation`); `false` from the moment it is turned off, including the grace window in which the retiring key still protects new writes (`keys[].active`).

keyConfigured.description: Whether this engine process holds the key-encryption key (`ENCRYPTION_KEY`). Without it, encryption cannot be turned on and no key can be added from this process.

keys.description: Every key that has ever protected `onboardings.context`, most recent first.

reencrypting.description: Whether an operator's request to re-encrypt every stored onboarding onto the active key is still outstanding. While it is, `progress.pending` counts rows on a superseded key as work; otherwise those rows are not pending, because rotation is lazy.

enabled.description: `true` turns encryption on — creating a first key if none is active — and encrypts every stored onboarding in the background; `false` turns it off, retires the active key, and decrypts every stored onboarding back to plain JSON in the background. Asking for the state that already holds changes nothing.

interval.description: How often the engine rotates the encryption key on its own, or `null` to stop rotating it automatically. Measured from the active key's creation rather than from this request, so an interval shorter than that key's current age makes it due at once. Required: turning the schedule off is `null`, never an omitted field.

id.description: The newly added key's id. Not active immediately — `GET /v1/admin/encryption` reports it as `pendingActivation` until `ENCRYPTION_KEY_RING_REFRESH_INTERVAL_MS` has elapsed.
